ontology.A_scenario: 3 agents × 3 simultaneous unit-demand tasks; N×K resources; C5 stationary all-tasks-present demand; competence profile is exogenous and paired across policies.
ontology.B_mechanism: Competencies are exogenous [0,1]-bounded two-regime processes. MIS-v2 and Nembhard are disabled. LinUCB learns reward-prediction parameters only; it does not change agent competence.
ontology.C_organization: Existing pairwise disjoint LinUCB scores are combined with either the existing bipartite optimizer or a deterministic online greedy matcher; fixed map is trained offline; dynamic true-mean oracle is evaluator-only.
ontology.policy_learning_vs_agent_learning: LinUCB model state updates from selected feedback; agent competence follows the seeded scenario process independently of decisions.

configuration.competence_transition: At each period after t=0, toggle stable/shifted regime with condition-specific probability p; geometric mean dwell is 1/p. C_t=C_base in stable regime; C_t=C_base+amplitude*S in shifted regime. Seeded and policy-independent.
configuration.demand: Existing N×K/C5 StationaryTaskDemand and generate_environment_trajectory_nk; all three task types are present each period, same seed/demand path for each policy and condition.
configuration.reward_observation: Bernoulli(mu) potential outcome for every pair-period, pre-generated from a separate coordinate-seeded stream and shared across policies and D conditions; selected policies receive only assigned-pair feedback.
configuration.contexts: One observed scalar context x[i,k,t]=C[i,k,t] per agent-task pair. For each pair, expected reward is linear theta*x with theta=1; LinUCB equations and alpha_from_delta(0.05) are unchanged.
configuration.resource_contract: Exactly three unit assignments per period; each agent and each task at most once; collective and individual unit capacity 1; equal resource use for all methods.
configuration.fixed_policy: Enumerate all 3! fixed task-to-agent maps and maximize total expected reward on 20 distinct 300-period training trajectories for each condition; test only on evaluation seeds.
configuration.compact_result_encoding: Each evaluation replication stores its exogenous regime path as 0/1 bits, each assignment as one digit 0–5 indexing the permutation list in this configuration, and each realized per-period reward as one digit 0–3. Aggregate time series and per-seed metrics are also stored; other period series are reproducible from the runner.
configuration.oracle: At each period maximize the evaluator-only true expected reward matrix using the existing bipartite optimizer. No policy sees the oracle or future regime path.
configuration.adaptation_cost: At each exogenous regime switch, report pseudo-regret and periods to first oracle matching in a predeclared window of at most 10 periods, truncated at the next switch or horizon.

limitations: Synthetic exogenous competence regimes are not industrial/empirical data and are not MIS-v2 or Nembhard learning.
The competence path is observed perfectly by both online LinUCB policies; no state-estimation error is tested.

The fixed baseline is trained with full expected-reward trajectories, while LinUCB observes selected pair outcomes only; this is intentionally a strong offline fixed comparator with a different training information budget.
The simultaneous LinUCB adapter applies multiple selected-pair updates per period; single-play LinUCB guarantees do not automatically apply.
The dynamic oracle is an evaluator-only true-mean reference, not an executable information-feasible policy.
Twenty evaluation seeds support a bounded sensitivity comparison, not a confirmatory generalization claim.
The change process is two-state Markov with specified mean dwell, not a deterministic periodic schedule; exact paths are seed-reproducible.
Computation times are local diagnostics, not portable runtime claims.
